# 4 Ezra Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — First dialogue

---

**3:1** In-the thirtieth year after the destruction of-the-city, I Salathiel — who-am also Ezra — was in-Babylon, and I lay upon my bed troubled, and my thoughts came-up over my heart,

**3:2** because I saw the desolation of-Zion and the wealth of-those who-dwell in-Babylon.

**3:3** And my spirit-was-greatly-agitated, so-that I began to speak anxious words before the Most-High,

**3:4** and I said: O LORD, you-who-dwell in-eternity, whose eyes are-exalted and whose upper-chambers are-in-the-air,

**3:5** whose throne is beyond-measure and whose glory is beyond comprehension, before-whom the host of-angels stands trembling,

**3:6** whose service is converted into wind and fire, whose word is true and utterances constant, whose ordinance is strong and commandment fearsome,

**3:7** whose look dries-up the depths and whose anger makes-the mountains-melt, and whose truth endures-forever:

**3:8** Hear, O LORD, the prayer of-your servant, and give-ear to-the petition of-your creature; give-heed to my words.

**3:9** For as-long-as I live I will-speak; and as-long-as I have-understanding I will-answer.

**3:10** Do-not-look upon-the sins of-your people, but upon-those who-served you in truth.

**3:11** Do-not-take-into-account the endeavors of-those who-practise wickedness, but upon-those who-kept your covenants in-affliction.

**3:12** Do-not-think-on-those who-walked in-wicked ways before-you, but remember those who-willingly acknowledged your fear.

**3:13** Let-it-not-be your will to-destroy those who-lived like cattle; but look-upon-those who-have-clearly taught your law.

**3:14** Do-not-be-angry with-those who-are deemed-worse-than animals, but love those who-always put their-trust in your righteousness and glory.

**3:15** For we and our fathers have-passed our lives in-ways that bring-death; but you, because of-us sinners, are-called merciful.

**3:16** For if-you desire to-have-mercy upon-us who-have no works of-righteousness, then you shall-be-called the-Merciful.

**3:17** For the righteous, who-have-many works stored-up with-you, shall-receive their reward in-consequence of-their own works.

**3:18** But what-is man, that you-are-angry with-him, or-what-is a corruptible race, that you-should-be bitter against-it?

**3:19** For in-truth there-is no one among those-born who-has not-sinned, and among those-who-have-existed there-is no one who-did-no-wrong.

**3:20** For in this, O LORD, your righteousness and goodness shall-be-declared, when you-are-merciful to those who-have no wealth of-good-works.

**3:21** Then I answered and said: You spoke at-the first, when you formed-the earth — and that alone — and commanded the dust,

**3:22** and Adam obeyed-you and you gave-him a living soul; and he was your workmanship and the work of-your hands, and you breathed into-him the breath of-life, and he was made-alive before-you.

**3:23** And you led-him into-paradise which your right-hand had-planted before-the earth appeared.

**3:24** And you charged-him [to observe] one commandment of-yours; but he transgressed-it, and immediately you appointed death for-him and for his generations; and from-him were-born nations and peoples and all tribes, of-which it-is not-possible to-count the multitude.

**3:25** And every nation walked after its-own will, and they behaved-wickedly before-you and despised your commandments, and you did-not-prevent-them.

**3:26** But again in-its-time you brought-the-flood upon the inhabitants of-the world and destroyed-them.

**3:27** And there-happened to-all of-them one and the-same fate — as death [came] upon Adam, so-the flood upon-them.

**3:28** But you-left one of-them — Noah with his household — all the-righteous ones who-descended from-him.

**3:29** And-it-came-to-pass that when the inhabitants of-the earth began-to-multiply, and children, nations, and many peoples increased, they began-again to-practise ungodliness, more than the-first.

**3:30** And when they-were-sinning before-you, you chose out one of-them, whose name was Abraham;

**3:31** and you loved-him, and to-him alone you revealed the end of-the times, secretly by-night.

**3:32** And you made with-him an everlasting covenant, and promised him that you-would-not forsake his seed forever.

**3:33** And you gave-him Isaac, and to Isaac you gave Jacob and Esau. And you set-apart Jacob for-yourself, but Esau you rejected; and Jacob became a great multitude.

**3:34** And when you led-his seed out of-Egypt, you brought-them to-mount Sinai.

**3:35** You bowed-down the-heavens, shook-the earth, moved-the world, made-the depths to-tremble, and troubled the-world.

**3:36** And your glory went-through four-gates of fire and earthquake and wind and ice, to-give the-law to-the seed of-Jacob, and the commandment to-the generation of-Israel.
